messages.content: You are a scientific agent. Analyze the compound scientifically and use the available information and tools to identify relevant transfer donors. You may select measured reference donors, never fabricate response values. Drug descriptions are pharmacology, not proof of context-specific response. No viability or causal claim. Return JSON only.

donors.reason: Exifone is a benzophenone polyphenol; high anchor similarity 0.6751 and structural similarity 0.2391 to gossypetin support histone-response transfer.
VU0155056 has highest anchor similarity 0.7001; retrieved source confirms naphthalenecarboxamide structure but no histone data.
Ruxolitinib has high anchor similarity 0.7003; retrieved source confirms kinase inhibitor pharmacology, not histone perturbation.
Ginkgetin is a biflavonoid with structural similarity 0.2537 to gossypetin; retrieved source supports flavonoid-related antineoplastic activity.

revised_hypotheses: Gossypetin's A375 histone profile is dominated by H3K27me1K36me2 loss (-2.366) and H3K56me0 gain (+1.1428), suggesting a reproducible chromatin perturbation if donor transfer preserves these directions.
High-anchor-similarity donors VU0155056, ruxolitinib, Exifone, and Ginkgetin are the strongest candidates for transferring a target-minus-A375 response matching gossypetin's histone marks.

Flavonoid/polyphenol donors Exifone and Ginkgetin may share chromatin-modifying effects with gossypetin, but retrieved sources provide only structural/pharmacological descriptions, not measured histone responses.
unresolved: No retrieved source provides measured histone mark responses for any donor, so donor support remains based on anchor similarity and structural/pharmacological description only.
KN-93 was not retrieved and is excluded despite anchor similarity 0.6625.
Whether any donor can produce a reproducible >0.5 log2 histone perturbation versus vehicle in the target context is not established.
